---
title: "MCU Design"
description: "Planned ADC/DMA acquisition, gap estimation, and hardware web interface."
---

## Revised Responsibilities

The STM32L432KC will acquire three MCP3204 channels: Hall A above the electromagnet, Hall B below it, and coil current. A timer starts 5 kHz SPI scans, with DMA moving the data. Every fifth scan supplies a 1 kHz calibrated gap estimate. Position PI executes on the FPGA.

The MCU sends estimated gap, requested gap, measured current, and status to the FPGA and receives telemetry. The revised protocol must also support coordinated PI-gain updates. Field layout, units, checks, acknowledgment, and timing remain to be specified; the existing eight-byte current-command packet is an earlier contract.

## Gap Estimate

Collect both Hall readings and current at independently measured gaps across 10–20 mm. Fit the estimator, then validate against separate measurements. Test current transients with the object fixed to detect false apparent motion.

The two Hall outputs use separate single-ended ADC conversions. Combine them in software rather than subtracting their mid-supply outputs directly with the ADC's restricted differential mode. See [resolution and calibration](design.qmd#resolution-and-calibration).

## Planned Hardware Webpage

Through the course ESP8266 and 125000-baud UART, the MCU will provide:

- Requested-gap control for the 10–20 mm demonstration range.
- A live graph of requested and estimated gap, with current and fault state visible.
- Position PI constant updates, with range checking and coordinated application at a control boundary.
- Stop and clear operating/fault status.

The proposal requires no visible latency during demonstration. Record actual display latency and loop timing under web traffic. This Quarto report site is separate from the hardware control page.

## Existing Sources and Bring-up

[main.c](firmware/src/main.c), [control.c](firmware/src/control.c), [board_stm32l432.c](firmware/src/board_stm32l432.c), [protocol.c](firmware/src/protocol.c), and [web.c](firmware/src/web.c) implement the earlier MCU-position/FPGA-current design. The live graph and FPGA position-PI gain controls are requirements, not verified features of those sources.

The standalone [one-byte SPI test](simple_byte/README.md) provides a smaller communication check. Its MCU Watch variable is `fpga_byte`; decimal 165 equals hexadecimal `0xA5`. A correct byte does not establish ADC/DMA timing or closed-loop operation.
